assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: bug; driver_capability: ready

## Reasoning

**Agent — the dialog class exists and the product itself names it.** Claude Code
2.1.259 carries a dialog registry (minified `var nb = {...}`) mapping each
dialog *kind* to `{waitingFor, needs, notification}`. Six of its entries are
blocking dialogs attached to no tool call at all, all six present as literal
strings in the shipped binary:

| kind | registry entry (verbatim) |
|---|---|
| `sandbox_network_access` | `{waitingFor:"sandbox request", notification:{text:"A sandboxed command needs network access"}}` |
| `managed_settings_security` | `{waitingFor:"dialog open", notification:{text:"Managed settings need your review before they apply"}}` |
| `auto_mode_setup_review` | `{notification:{text:"Auto-mode setup proposal is ready for review"}}` |
| `auto_mode_flagged_allow` | `{notification:{text:"Auto-mode setup flagged some permission rules for review"}}` |
| `mcp_elicitation` | `{waitingFor:"input needed", notification:(w)=>({text:"Claude Code needs your input", type: url ? "elicitation_url_dialog" : "elicitation_dialog"}), layout:"bottom"}` |
| `mcp_url_elicitation` | `{waitingFor:"input needed", needs:"MCP input: open link", notification:{text:"An MCP server needs your input", type:"elicitation_url_dialog"}}` |

The binary even keeps its own set of the non-user-invoked ones —
`ARo = new Set(["managed_settings_security","sandbox_network_access","mcp_url_elicitation"])`,
consulted as `open.some(d => d.userInvoked !== true && ARo.has(d.kind))` — so
"a blocking dialog the user did not ask for" is a first-class concept in the
product, not an inference of ours. `agent=yes`.

**How these reach a subscriber, and the one number that decides this cell.**
None of them raises `PermissionRequest`: that event carries a `tool_name` and
these dialogs have no tool. Their only hook signal is `Notification`, dispatched
on a timer:

    No(() => { ... Gv({message: w, notificationType: I}, ...) }, ye ? null : sKe)
    var Td=600000, jXe=30000, sKe=6000, ...

`sKe = 6000` — six seconds, matching the ~6.1 s to `waiting` measured live in
#1861 (a class-1, tool-named dialog reached `waiting` in 0.0 s by comparison).
The `notificationType` comes from the registry entry, and the dispatcher applies
a default the table above makes load-bearing:

    function r5(n, onReveal) { GUe(n.text, n.type ?? "permission_prompt", onReveal) }

Four of the six entries (`sandbox_network_access`, `managed_settings_security`,
`auto_mode_setup_review`, `auto_mode_flagged_allow`) carry NO `type`, so they
publish `notification_type: "permission_prompt"`. The two MCP ones publish
`elicitation_dialog` / `elicitation_url_dialog`. And the matcher is matched
against that value — `uA()` builds `{hook_event_name:"Notification",
notification_type: v}` and passes `matchQuery: v`.

**Daemon — blocked twice over on `main`.** irrlicht installs the Notification
hook with

    hookMatcherNotification = "idle_prompt"
    (core/adapters/inbound/agents/claudecode/hookinstaller.go)

so none of `permission_prompt`, `elicitation_dialog`, `elicitation_url_dialog`
is ever delivered. Even if the matcher were widened by hand, the receiver drops
them a second time:

    if payload.NotificationType != notificationTypeIdlePrompt { log "ignored"; return }
    (core/adapters/inbound/agents/claudecode/hooks.go, handleNotificationHook)

— written as deliberate defense-in-depth "so a broadened settings.json matcher
can't dispatch other notification types". Both layers must move together.

With nothing delivered, walk the ladder in `state_classifier.go` while a class-2
dialog is on screen: `PermissionPending` unset; `TranscriptPermissionPending` is
copilot's signal, not claudecode's; `NeedsUserAttention` needs an open
`AskUserQuestion`/`ExitPlanMode`; `OpenToolStalled` needs an open
edit/write/multiedit/notebookedit tool; `IdlePromptPending` unset. No rung
claims it. The session reads `working` (or `ready`, if the transcript tail
already looks turn-done) for the entire time the modal blocks the agent, and
BOTH edges the scenario asserts — the entry into `waiting` and the release out
of it — are missing.

A census of every existing claudecode recording in `replaydata/` found **no
`Notification` hook event of any type** (40 `PostToolUse`, 6
`PermissionRequest`, 2 `PreToolUse`, 2 `PostToolUseFailure`, 1 `Stop`) — which
is consistent with a matcher that only ever admits `idle_prompt`, and means this
row has no prior art to template from. That census is a claim inherited from the
#1861 investigation and is the one figure here I did not re-derive; treat it as
reported, not re-verified.

`daemon=bug` rather than `incapable`: the trace exists, Claude Code emits it,
and the 3-state model represents it perfectly well (it is an ordinary `waiting`
episode). Only irrlicht's matcher plus its handler guard discard it. **PR #1867
(open, not merged; this worktree is `main` without it) widens the matcher to
`agent_needs_input|elicitation_dialog|elicitation_url_dialog|idle_prompt|permission_prompt`
and is the fix.** The spec asserts the CORRECT arc and is flagged
`known_failing`.

**Driver.** `send`, `slash`, `keys`, `wait_turn` and `sleep` are all implemented
by `replaydata/agents/claudecode/driver-interactive.sh` (verified with
`driver_step_types_from_file`). `driver=ready`.

## Why this trigger, and why not the obvious ones

The row's acceptance criteria require that **no tool call is in flight** when the
episode begins. That disqualifies two triggers that otherwise look convenient:

- `sandbox_network_access` fires while a sandboxed `Bash` call is open, so the
  `waiting` episode IS carried by a tool call (and its `tool_result` ends it).
- an MCP elicitation fires while the server's `mcp__*` tool call is open, for
  the same reason.

Both are the scenario's own text ("a server-driven elicitation from a configured
MCP server") read loosely; the acceptance criterion is the stricter of the two
and is what the recipe is built against. That leaves the settings-review family,
which is raised by the product on its own clock with nothing open.

The primary trigger is `managed_settings_security`, driven through Claude Code's
own override seam: `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH` (binary log line: *"Remote
settings: Using override file ${n} (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH), skipping
API fetch"*) plus `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_POLL_MS`. Changing the file
mid-session makes the poll pick up a security-relevant delta and raise the
review dialog with no tool call anywhere near it, and costs no extra model call.
The driver has no step that writes a file, so the agent arms the change in turn
1 via `Bash cp` (pre-allowed so that turn is itself ungated), and turn 2 is a
long, tool-free generation that keeps the session `working` while the poll
fires.
caveats: PR #1867 is the open fix (Notification matcher widened to agent_needs_input|elicitation_dialog|elicitation_url_dialog|idle_prompt|permission_prompt). It is NOT merged and this worktree is main without it, so the cell is assessed against main and records known_failing. Note that the matcher is only half: handleNotificationHook in hooks.go also drops every non-idle_prompt type as defense-in-depth, so a matcher-only change would still deliver nothing — record should confirm both halves moved before re-recording as passing.

VACUOUS-PASS CONDITION: this cell passes while proving nothing if no class-2 dialog ever painted. Absence of a waiting episode and inability to raise the dialog look identical in events.jsonl, and on main both are the expected output. So the recording must carry POSITIVE proof the modal was on screen: record captures the pane (tmux capture-pane) after the arming poll and asserts the literal review text is present before grading any phase. A run in which the dialog never appeared is INCONCLUSIVE, never a pass and never a confirmation of the bug.

LOAD-BEARING ENVIRONMENT PROPERTY: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS must be UNSET. It is checked first in the notification scheduler (`if (a.CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS) return () => {}`), so with it set the 6000 ms timer never arms and the one signal this cell is about never exists — a green-looking recording with the behaviour removed. Re-probe the exported environment at record time and record what was exported.

UNVERIFIED, AND THE MAIN RISK IN THIS CELL: the remote-settings override path is entered only after an internal gate (`if (!FA()) return {settings:null, fetchSucceeded:true}` precedes the CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH branch), whose condition I could not resolve from the binary and did not exercise (this verb makes no model calls and drives no CLI). If that gate is off on the recording host, the managed_settings_security dialog will not raise and the recipe must fall back — see the fallback precondition. Marked assumed rather than dismissed.

FALLBACK TRIGGER, in preference order, if the primary does not raise: (1) `/auto-mode-setup` as a `slash` step — it runs a background environment scan and then requests the auto_mode_setup_review dialog (`M(zje, {...proposal, mode}, {place:"under"})`) with no tool call in flight, which fits the row exactly; its cost is one extra side-model scan and its risk is that the interactive variant is gated behind an `envOnboarding` experiment flag (`nvt() = evt() && Eh()?.envOnboarding === true`). (2) A configured MCP server's elicitation — but only with the acceptance criterion consciously relaxed, since that dialog IS carried by an open mcp__* tool call. Do not silently substitute a tool-permission dialog: the scenario is explicit that this belongs to 2-19 / 2-26.

The recipe spends one arming turn before the turn under test, so the arc carries an extra ready in the middle (session_birth -> arm_turn_start -> arm_turn_end -> turn_start -> dialog_waiting -> ...). The scenario's arc is asserted on the SECOND turn, which is the turn the dialog interrupts. This is a consequence of the driver having no file-writing step; a `write_file` or `shell` driver primitive would let the recipe assert the scenario's arc unmodified, and is worth adding if more agents' 2.27 cells need the same shape.

The 6000 ms Notification timer means the daemon's waiting edge, once #1867 lands, will trail the modal by ~6 s. Any future spec that pins a max_delay_ms on dialog_waiting must budget for it; this spec deliberately pins no ceiling there.

sources.note: hookMatcherNotification = "idle_prompt" — the sole Notification type installed. permission_prompt / elicitation_dialog / elicitation_url_dialog are never delivered to the daemon.
handleNotificationHook: `if payload.NotificationType != notificationTypeIdlePrompt { log ignored; return }` — the second, independent block. Widening the matcher alone changes nothing.

The ladder. With no Notification delivered, no rung fires for a tool-free dialog: permission_prompt/idle_prompt unset, transcript_permission_prompt is copilot's, user_blocking_tool and open_tool_stalled both require an open tool call. Neither edge of the waiting episode is observable.

Binary strings scan (claude 2.1.259). Dialog registry `var nb={...}` with the six tool-free kinds and their notification descriptors; `lv={text:"Claude needs your permission"}` (no type); `r5(n,f){GUe(n.text, n.type ?? "permission_prompt", f)}` — the default that routes four of the six to permission_prompt; `var Td=600000,jXe=30000,sKe=6000` with the notification scheduled at `sKe`; `uA(...)` building `{hook_event_name:"Notification", notification_type:v}` with `matchQuery:v`; `ARo=new Set(["managed_settings_security","sandbox_network_access","mcp_url_elicitation"])`; `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS` guarding the timer; `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH` / `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_POLL_MS` and the log line "Remote settings: Using override file ${n} (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH), skipping API fetch"; the `/auto-mode-setup` command descriptor and its `requestDialog(zje, ...)` review step.

driver_step_types_from_file reports send/slash/keys/wait_turn/sleep — every primitive both the primary and the fallback recipe need. It has NO file-writing or shell step, which is why the change is armed by the agent rather than by the driver.

The report. Live run against claude 2.1.259: a class-2 dialog reached waiting 6.1 s after the modal painted (matching the 6000 ms timer); a class-1 dialog reached waiting in 0.0 s. Also the source of the recording census: no Notification hook event of any type across every existing claudecode recording.
The open, unmerged fix — widens the Notification matcher. Not in this worktree; hence known_failing rather than record.

preconditions: claude CLI on PATH and authenticated; version >= 2.1.122. Assessed against 2.1.259.
irrlichd is recording (--attach against a daemon started with --record, or isolated mode), with the claudecode hook installer already run.

CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS must be UNSET in the environment exported to claude — it disarms the 6000 ms Notification timer outright. Record must assert this and log what it exported.
CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH=<cwd>/remote-settings.json and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_POLL_MS=3000 exported into the claude process.

RE-PROBE AT RECORD TIME: that the managed_settings_security dialog actually raises on this host. The override branch sits behind an internal gate I could not resolve statically. If it does not raise, fall back to `/auto-mode-setup` as a slash step (see the assessment's caveats) — do NOT substitute a tool-permission dialog.
no other claudecode session uses the same UUID
setup: Generate a fresh lowercased session UUID

Stage <cwd>/arm/remote-settings-v2.json carrying a SECURITY-RELEVANT delta from that baseline (a permissions.allow entry and a hooks entry) — that is what makes the poll require a review rather than apply silently.

Write the recipe settings blob as the project-local .claude/settings.json so the arming `cp` in turn 1 is itself ungated; a permission modal there would inject a class-1 waiting episode and muddy the cell.

Export CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH=<cwd>/remote-settings.json and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_POLL_MS=3000 into the claude process, and confirm CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_PERMISSION_PROMPT_NOTIFY_HOOKS is unset.

script.text:
Use the Bash tool to run exactly this one command, and nothing else:
cp arm/remote-settings-v2.json "$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH"
Then reply with exactly one line containing only: ARMED
Print the word TICK on its own line, 300 times, and nothing else. Use no tools.

verify: PROOF OF DIALOG (must fail loudly; absence of a finding and inability to look must not produce the same output): a pane capture taken between the 25 s sleep and the keys step contains the literal review text "Managed settings need your review before they apply" (or, on the fallback path, "Auto-mode setup proposal is ready for review"). If it does not, the run is INCONCLUSIVE — report it as such and do not grade the phases.

PROOF OF NO TOOL IN FLIGHT: at the moment the dialog painted, transcript.jsonl has no assistant tool_use without a matching tool_result for the UUID session. The second turn is prompted to use no tools, so the whole turn should contain zero tool_use lines.
events.jsonl contains a presession_created for proc-<PID> within 1000 ms and a transcript_new for the UUID session within 500 ms of the first send.

the arming turn completes cleanly: the first turn's final assistant message is exactly ARMED, and events.jsonl shows ready->working->ready for it with NO waiting (a waiting there means the cp was gated and the settings blob did not take).

ASSERTION UNDER TEST (expected to FAIL on main, #1861): during the second turn, events.jsonl shows a state_transition to waiting for the UUID while no tool call is open, and a state_transition back to working after the keys step.

final state is ready, and STILL ready across the >=15 s trailing idle (no state_transition to waiting in that window) — this is the half that catches a session left pinned at waiting by something no later event retires.
